accounting_crosswalk.caveat: Circle's blog rounds a combined $819M partner-and-transaction figure. The 10-Q distinguishes $815.8M distribution and transaction costs, $819.3M including other costs, and $655.3M Coinbase-related distribution costs. The $819M is not all paid to Coinbase or necessarily all paid to partners.

circle_h1_2026.capital_boundary: Gross onchain volume and gross two-way mint/redemption are not net issuance, new external capital or unique settlement. No route-level external-settlement breakdown is supplied.

circle_binance.agreement_focus: Expand USDC access and promotion, especially across emerging markets.
circle_binance.circle_role: Provide infrastructure services supporting holding and use of USDC.
circle_binance.binance_role: Promote, increase awareness and integrate USDC on its platform.
circle_binance.share_transfer_restriction: Circle's announcement says Binance agreed not to transfer the shares for up to two years from closing, subject to customary exceptions.
circle_binance.xrp_relationship: Indirect market-structure connection only. Binance is an XRP venue; the disclosed investment and commercial agreement focus on USDC. No XRP-specific investment, purchase commitment or XRP settlement agreement is disclosed.

observations.caveat: Liquidation feed is partial; account ratio is not notional exposure.

observations.caveat: Page did not expose exact refresh time. Coinbase is a provider venue label, not Coinbase corporate proprietary holdings or customer net exposure.

derived.interpretation: A material portion of the $2.69B versus $1.63B gap is explained by product scope: TRdesk includes quarterly futures while Bentley explicitly excludes them. Venue coverage also differs (26 vs 17 vs 7). Residual provider/API inclusion differences remain unreconciled.
derived.admission_rule: Retain provider-specific timestamps, venues and contract scope. Do not average or treat open interest as net capital inflow.

xrp_derivatives.positioning_interpretation: Positive funding and a long-heavy account distribution are crowding-risk features, not a directional forecast. Open interest counts outstanding matched contracts once and always has both a long and short side.

macro_geopolitical_context.reported_event: Reuters reported on November 2 that oil fell more than 6% amid reports of Iran-Qatar talks aimed at ending the US-Israeli war involving Iran; it also reported a 76.6% market-implied probability of a December Fed rate hike, down from 80% one week earlier.
macro_geopolitical_context.xrp_causal_status: No direct XRP causal effect established. Use as event context for energy, inflation, rates and risk appetite, not a standalone XRP signal.

hypotheses.claim: The five-year Binance-USDC agreement could increase USDC use on corridors where XRP bridge liquidity competes.
hypotheses.support: Official $100M equity investment and USDC commercial agreement; Binance is also a major XRP venue.

hypotheses.claim: USDC distribution may complement XRP by expanding a multi-asset exchange ecosystem.
hypotheses.support: Binance supports both USDC and XRP; no exclusivity disclosed.
hypotheses.counter: No route-level customer or settlement data.

hypotheses.claim: A material part of OI disagreement reflects different contract scope and venue inclusion rather than a sudden capital movement.
hypotheses.support: Bentley excludes quarterlies; TRdesk includes quarterlies and perps.

hypotheses.claim: Positive funding and long-heavy accounts may increase liquidation sensitivity if price moves against longs.
hypotheses.support: TradRadar funding +0.0076%/8h and 78.1% long accounts; reported liquidations predominantly long.
hypotheses.counter: No complete liquidation feed, position-size distribution, depth or calibrated conditional model.
